stem:
Qadir leaves a bowl of plain cooked dal uncovered in warm air. Beside it, a jar of mango pickle made with plenty of salt stays fresh for months.

Which statement best explains why the dal spoils but the pickle does not get infected in the same way?

options.text: Microorganisms from the air settle on the exposed dal and spoil it, while enough salt in the pickle acts as a preservative.
Even a tiny amount of salt would keep the dal from spoiling.
The dal rots first, and that rotting produces the microorganisms.
The pickle cannot get infected, even without enough salt, because it is a pickle.

teacher.key_rationale: Microbes from surroundings spoil exposed dal; high salt preserves the pickle. A tiny amount of salt is not enough; rotting does not create the microbes first; the food name alone does not protect without enough salt.

mx_swap.reason: Air-only-no-rot CWO fights the stem's warm-air spoilage setup; kept condition_omission, relationship_reversal, and surface_feature_capture.
